#; Tag#: 05.44.46.0009
#; Issue#: IB14740272
#; Severity: Medium
#; Category: CPU
#; Symptom: (ITS:102426) There is warning message about "XX.55 No irq handler for vector"(XX is CPU thread#) in Linux dmesg log
#;          ,during AC on/off longrun cycles. Fail rate 1/200 - 1/700.
#; RootCause: By inference, during the course of POST, the AP's were exposed to ExtINT/INTR events as a result of this misconfiguration 
#;            (probably due to the UEFI timer-tick using the 8259), and this left a pending ExtINT/INTR interrupt latched on the AP's.
#;            When the AP's are started by the OS, the latched ExtINT/INTR interrupt is processed shortly after the OS 
#;            enabled interrupts on the core by setting the EFLAGS.IF bit. The AP's CPU core then queried the 8259 to 
#;            identify the vector number (which is the value of the 8259's ICW2 register + the IRQ level). 
#;            The master 8259's ICW2 was set to 0x30, and since no 8259 interrupts are pending, the 8259 will respond 
#;            with a IRQ7 (spurious interrupt) yielding a vector of 0x37 or decimal 55.
#; Description: (Bug Fix)
#; Solution: Refer to kernel code base, using HPET timer for UEFI timer-tick.
#; SolutionDependency: none
#; Reviewer: IB14740000
#; RelatedFiles:
#; Added:
#;   1. AMD\AmdEmbedded\AmdCommonChipsetPkg\Override\
#;   2. AMD\AmdEmbedded\AmdCommonChipsetPkg\Override\EDK2\
